title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.32
exact_target: Decide whether a finite group occurs as the commutator subgroup of a finite group, and determine the computational complexity of doing so.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 2541 (KOU-21.32). CC BY 4.0.

P. J. Cameron, Problem 21.32, in E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), \emph{The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory}, 21st edition, arXiv:1401.0300v48 (6 October 2026). This version records decidability and a complexity result; the displayed question is the historically registered target.

Sathasivam Kalithasan and Viji Z. Thomas, \emph{On the decidability of the integrability of finite groups}, arXiv:2602.18829v1 (2026), Introduction, main theorem and corollary. It proves decidability by a computable finite order bound.
